images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A heavy desk stapler about the length of a pencil rests on an ivory card blotter at the front of a pale neutral tabletop. Its upper arm is acid-lime enamel, the one lime element, over a brushed graphite base with a visible hinge pin. A crisp, pencil-thin graphite outline traced on the blotter marks its proper spot exactly. Behind it, a row of three miniature graphite desks recedes toward the back of the table, and on the right a narrow frosted acrylic stairwell model steps down out of frame. A folded ivory jacket hangs over the nearest desk chair, left by someone gone to lunch. Fine eraser crumbs and a few stray staples sit on the blotter, and dust softens the outline's edge. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

The outline on the blotter is now empty, and the lime stapler has been pushed away across the whole layout. A skid trail of scuffed graphite marks and scattered staples runs from the outline past each desk, where boxes of papers have been dumped to fill its place. The stapler is frozen mid-tumble at the top of the frosted stairwell, tilted nose-down over the first step, its arm flipped open and a spray of loose staples hanging in the air below it. At the foot of the stairs, a dim graphite storage shelf is crammed with other displaced desk objects, a graphite tape dispenser and a frosted glass mug among them. The ivory jacket has slid off its chair onto the floor. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: the same soft upper-left key and right-side bounce fill as a calm studio setup, unchanged, so the disorder reads as physical and real rather than theatrical. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A flooded basement ruin spreads wide and low, still grey water reaching to a far row of cracked frosted-glass block pillars fading into haze. Islands of rubble break the surface: a toppled graphite storage shelf the size of a building, a sunken frosted mug, drifts of soggy ivory boxes slumping into the water. Snapped desk frames stand in lines like old piers. Near the centre, on a raised graphite landing, the old stapler sits weathered and pale, its paint worn back to bare metal. A slim graphite lift mast rises from the landing up through a broken slab toward a shaft of daylight, and its acid-lime platform has just cradled the stapler and begun to climb, water dripping from its underside. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents.
